rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding discussion can produce disbelief and malice only in people with no potential; the coming verses should be read against this background.
rows.anchor: produce scrubs and weeds of disbelief and malice in those who do not have the slightest potential.

rows.speaker: The Arabs
rows.claim: The Arabs accepted God as creator of the heavens, earth, and all things while also setting up other deities beside Him.
rows.anchor: The Arabs believed that the heavens and the earth and all other things have been created by God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Arabs assigned cosmic spheres to God's workers, treating them as final authorities, necessary means of access to God, and providers of sustenance, wealth, and children.
rows.anchor: Now, it was these workers who hold the final authority in their respective spheres.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Arabs doctrinally affirmed God as creator and supreme deity, in practice they centered worship on His deputies as deities and intercessors.
rows.anchor: Though ideologically they believed that God was the creator and the supreme deity, practically all their association was not with Him but with His deputies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes them: since their Lord is the creator of the heavens and earth and they acknowledge no other creator, why assign partners to Him?
rows.anchor: the Almighty has chided them by saying that the creator of the heavens and the earth is precisely their Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six creation days are divine days or phases, not ordinary twenty-four-hour days.
rows.anchor: The days referred to in the verse are not the twenty four hour days.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an describes divine days as spanning a thousand or fifty thousand earthly years.
rows.anchor: these days can be equal to a thousand earth years (32:5) as well as fifty thousand earth years (70:4).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah and Qur'an both describe creation in six phases, and modern philosophy likewise reinforces gradual creation, so ancient and modern views do not conflict on this point.
rows.anchor: The Torah and the Qur’ ān both mention the world being created in six phases.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evolution as its advocates present it has many gaps; those gaps cannot be filled without accepting the Qur'an's logical and natural principles, which he will explain elsewhere.
rows.anchor: the way advocates present the theory of evolution there are many gaps in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could have created the universe instantly by command, but His wisdom entailed its creation through six phases.
rows.anchor: This was not beyond His power. However, His wisdom entailed that it be created in six phases.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation's gradual stages manifest God's wisdom, providence, and mercy alongside His power; these manifestations complete human intellectual and spiritual development.
rows.anchor: Their manifestation is as important for the completion of intellectual and spiritual aspects of a person as is that of the completion of power of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As he explains in Sūrah al-Anʿām, God could send bread directly, yet winds, clouds, rain, cultivation, and harvest reveal His creativity, governance, power, and wisdom in every part of creation.
rows.anchor: a treasure of the signs of God’s creativity and governance and of His marvels of power and wisdom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many transformations of a single object attract attention, letting people recognize God's signs and learn from them.
rows.anchor: A single object changes form and shape in so many ways in order to attract our attention

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A smallest particle mirrors the universe: its creator gradually completes it through phases until it has the features needed for human life.
rows.anchor: until finally it was accorded all the features necessary for human life to thrive.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This gradual creation is neither accident nor amusement; it is purposeful, and its purpose will necessarily appear one day.
rows.anchor: shows that it has a purpose to it, which will one day necessarily manifest itself.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ascension to the throne follows from His majestic creation: creating the universe entails governing it, rather than leaving it unattended.
rows.anchor: How is it possible that God becomes unconcerned about its governance after creating it?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne statement refutes both idolaters who assigned administration to associates and philosophers who treat God as a first cause unconcerned with creation's consequences.
rows.anchor: a refutation of those shallow philosophers who regard God to be the first cause

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for throne signifies political authority; istawā following ʿalā means to sit and take charge.
rows.anchor: the throne) signifies political authority. When 6  is used after

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term rendered “fervour” explains the governance and planning implied by taking charge: the universe moves by its creator's plan, and heavenly bodies follow fixed paths without deviation.
rows.anchor: The implication is that the movement going on the system of this universe is because of this governance and planning of the creator.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the creator can issue commands: everything follows God's command with zeal and efficiency, which is fitting for it.
rows.anchor: Who else can give commands than the one who creates?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rendered “fervour” shows that all things carry out God's orders zealously, without hesitation; humans should worship and obey their creator.
rows.anchor: There is not the slightest hesitancy anywhere.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage mentions the night’s zeal but not the day's because it mentions the sun after the night.
rows.anchor: here sun has been mentioned after the night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form tafāʿul is emphatic hyperbole, making tabāraka mean that God is very blessed and merciful.
rows.anchor: The form tafā‘ul has extreme exaggeration in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe testifies not only to God's power and exaltedness but also to His providence, mercy, and benevolence.
rows.anchor: His providence, mercy and benevolence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse counters idolatrous nations' belief that God's loftiness and power overshadow His mercy, making access to Him seem impossible and prompting mediation.
rows.anchor: they increased the extent of God’s loftiness and power so much that His mercy and blessings were sidelined as a result.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters imagined angels as God's favoured daughters and sought to please them so that they would win their father's favour and intercession.
rows.anchor: thinking that they were favoured daughters of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the universe shows God's power and boundless mercy, there is no need for mediation; people should call upon Him alone in hope or despair.
rows.anchor: there is no need to find a means or some mediation to ask from Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term translated “beseeching” means humility and coaxing, expressed through both words and actions; the best expression combines both.
rows.anchor: The best form of this is the prayer ritual.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khafiyah means “secretly”; private supplication promotes sincerity and faithfulness by protecting against show, and God's hearing makes shouting unnecessary.
rows.anchor: means “secretly.” It is a mannerism of humility which also ensures the elements of sincerity and faithfulness in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Secretly” closes the door to pomp and bad manners and stresses moderation, while allowing occasional loud personal or congregational supplication.
rows.anchor: This does not negate the loud tone a person may sometimes adopt in his individual supplications or collective ones in a congregation.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that God alone creates and governs, the passage states the creature's duty: invoke and beseech Him alone in secret, without arrogance.
rows.anchor: they must beseech and invoke Him only in secret.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because every part of the universe submits fervently to God, humans have no right to arrogance; God dislikes those who exceed limits.
rows.anchor: Every object of this universe is in submission to God and is fervently carrying out His orders.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe and world history show that God keeps things within limits and does not let the arrogant pass their appointed limit.
rows.anchor: world history too bears witness that He did not give the arrogant respite beyond a certain limit.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command against spreading disorder negatively restates the preceding demand for exclusive worship: one divine will preserves cosmic order, whereas other deities would disrupt it.
rows.anchor: The only reason this world is intact is that only the single intent of God prevails in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unity of God's rule in the ordained sphere entails exclusive worship and obedience in human affairs; associating others disrupts justice and peace, creating anarchy and rebellion.
rows.anchor: human beings too should worship and obey the one and only God in their own circle of authority

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “after it has been set right” intensifies the crime: disrupting an already ordered land is graver than disturbing an already disordered state.
rows.anchor: it becomes graver if this is done after its affairs have been set right.
